note: One real instance of every problem code, produced by running the named function over a document that provokes it. The `message` strings are verbatim: the canvas renders them unaltered, so a client test asserting against a paraphrase would be asserting about a fiction.

instances.scenario: four loops against the cycle ceiling, one of them from a plain agent
instances.why: `back-edge-not-router` is the measured one: with a plain node closing the loop the join fires once, the second arrival is suppressed, and the run ends normally having produced nothing - no exception, no warning.

problem.message: edge 'e9' closes a loop from 'b' back to 'a', and 'b' is a agent node. A loop-closing node MUST be a router: insert a router node between 'b' and 'a' and draw the back edge from that router instead. This is measured, not cautious - with a plain node here the join fires once, the second arrival is suppressed, and the run ends normally having produced nothing, with no exception and no warning

instances.scenario: more model-calling nodes than the billable ceiling

problem.message: this graph has 14 nodes that call a model and the ceiling is 13 (MAX_BILLABLE_NODES), which is the shipped validator's 8 with the same 1.7 headroom MAX_GRAPH_NODES applies. This bound is about shape rather than spend - what a graph COSTS is checked separately, against the per-run ceiling, and that check names a dollar figure you can act on

instances.scenario: a graph whose worst case prices past the per-run ceiling

problem.message: this graph's worst case prices at $8.24 over 288 model calls, and $10.30 with the 1.25x margin, against a per-run ceiling of $10.00. Remove a node that calls a model, move one to the cheap tier, take a node off a cycle, or lower a retry ceiling

instances.scenario: a tier pointed at a model PRICES cannot price
instances.why: Provoked by pointing the cheap tier at a slug with no PRICES entry, which is the shape a model swap without a matching price commit takes. The failure it stands against is the one that reported a 128,069-token run at $0.00: `PRICES.get(model, (0.0, 0.0))` turning 'no price on file' into 'this call was free'.

problem.message: this graph cannot be priced: openrouter/example/unpriced-preview has no entry in PRICES, so every call it makes would contribute $0.00 to a total that is supposed to bound spend. Add the price in the same commit as the model

instances.scenario: four loops against the cycle ceiling, one of them from a plain agent
instances.why: `back-edge-not-router` is the measured one: with a plain node closing the loop the join fires once, the second arrival is suppressed, and the run ends normally having produced nothing - no exception, no warning.

problem.message: this graph closes 4 loops and the ceiling is 3 (MAX_CYCLES), the validator's own measured back-edge count. Each loop multiplies the price of every node inside it

instances.scenario: a gate allowing more revise turns than the cycle-iteration ceiling

problem.message: gate 'confirm' allows 4 revise turns and the ceiling is 3 (MAX_CYCLE_ITERATIONS), because a revise loop is a cycle and every node on one is billed again each time round. It is deliberately below the validator's own 5: that number prices a human in the loop, who is both the cause of the delay and the brake on it, and a builder cycle need not have one

instances.scenario: two nodes and two edges sharing an id

problem.message: 2 edges share the id 'e1'; ids address a node in every frame, every edge and every problem message, so they must be unique

instances.scenario: two nodes and two edges sharing an id

problem.message: 2 nodes share the id 'step'; ids address a node in every frame, every edge and every problem message, so they must be unique

instances.scenario: an edge arriving at the input node

problem.message: edge 'e2' arrives at 'idea', which is the graph's input: an input node starts the run and has nothing upstream of it

instances.scenario: an edge naming a node that was deleted

problem.message: edge 'e2' names 'ghost' as its target, and no node has that id

instances.scenario: an edge leaving an agent by a gate's port

problem.message: edge 'e2' leaves 'draft' by the port 'approve', and a agent node offers out

instances.scenario: more escalation-tier nodes than the escalation ceiling

problem.message: this graph puts 9 nodes on the escalation tier and the ceiling is 8 (MAX_ESCALATION_NODES), the validator's own measured split of 5 escalation to 3 cheap carried up by the same headroom as the node count. Move one to the cheap tier

instances.scenario: one node fanning out wider than the concurrency ceiling

problem.message: 'idea' fans out to 5 nodes and the ceiling is 4 (MAX_FANOUT_WIDTH), the validator's own measured maximum. What this bounds is concurrent branches, and the real constraint behind it is GitHub's 10 requests a minute per IP

instances.scenario: a router declaring the same branch label twice
instances.why: The two codes come from one mistake, and `ident-collision` comes from nothing else. Method idents are n<index>_<id> and event labels e<index>_<port>, and the index is unique per node, so the ONLY way two compiled names collide is a router emitting one label twice - which is what a duplicate branch is.

problem.message: 2 nodes compile to the same router label 'e1_same'; frames from both would attribute to one node

instances.scenario: a gate whose id leaves no room for its compiled router

problem.message: 'gaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaa' compiles to the flow method 'n2_route_gaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaa', which does not match ^n[0-9]{1,2}_[a-z0-9_]{1,40}$. A gate compiles to two methods and the second is prefixed 'route_', so a gate's id has six characters less room than any other node's; shorten it

instances.scenario: two input nodes asking for the same key

problem.message: 2 input nodes both ask for 'idea'; the run request carries one value under that name and there would be no saying which node it seeded

instances.scenario: an input node asking for a different key than the document declares

problem.message: the document declares input_field 'idea' and no input node asks for it; the input nodes ask for topic

instances.scenario: joins naming a node that is not there, and one with a single arrival

problem.message: 'step' is declared a join and 1 edge(s) arrive at it. A join over one edge is the same as no join at all

instances.scenario: joins naming a node that is not there, and one with a single arrival

problem.message: joins names 'ghost', and no node has that id

instances.scenario: an agent whose task placeholders are left unfilled

problem.message: draft runs 'scoper', whose task needs human_override, idea and this node does not supply them

instances.scenario: a crew that is registered but cannot be constructed
instances.why: `SynthesisCrew` takes typed findings at construction, so a document naming it once compiled, published and priced cleanly and then raised a bare TypeError at the first PAID run - after the scoper and all three research branches had billed.

problem.message: combine: the crew 'synthesis' cannot be built from a document: SynthesisCrew requires market, sentiment, feasibility at construction, and those are typed findings the validator flow hands over in Python rather than anything a drawn graph can supply. The crews a document may name are feasibility, market, scope, sentiment

instances.scenario: an agent naming a library id this deployment does not register

problem.message: draft names the agent 'nobody'; the registered agents are feasibility_analyst, market_analyst, reporter, scoper, sentiment_analyst, synthesist

instances.scenario: a graph with nothing to seed it

problem.message: this graph has no input node, so there is nothing to seed a run with and no field for the run request to carry

instances.scenario: an input node asking for a different key than the document declares

problem.message: this graph has no output node, so a completed run hands back no body. Everything it produced would be visible only as streamed frames

instances.scenario: more nodes than the graph ceiling

problem.message: this graph has 26 nodes and the ceiling is 24 (MAX_GRAPH_NODES); above that a single pass of the graph no longer fits comfortably in the 2,000-frame replay ring, and a reconnecting client would receive an incomplete run with nothing saying so

instances.scenario: a node nothing leads to

problem.message: nothing leads to 'stranded' from an input node, so it can never run. Connect it, or delete it

instances.scenario: a router with five branches and no otherwise

problem.message: router 'wide' declares 5 branches; a router takes 2 to 4. Fewer than 2 is a decision that cannot go either way, and more than 4 crosses MAX_FANOUT_WIDTH

instances.scenario: a router with five branches and no otherwise

problem.message: router 'wide' declares the branch 'five' and no edge leaves by it, so a run taking that branch stops here. That is legal - it is how a graph ends early - but it is rarely intended

instances.scenario: a router declaring the same branch label twice
instances.why: The two codes come from one mistake, and `ident-collision` comes from nothing else. Method idents are n<index>_<id> and event labels e<index>_<port>, and the index is unique per node, so the ONLY way two compiled names collide is a router emitting one label twice - which is what a duplicate branch is.

problem.message: router 'pick' declares the branch 'same' 2 times; a branch label is the port an edge leaves by, so a duplicate makes the drawn edge ambiguous

instances.scenario: a router with five branches and no otherwise

problem.message: router 'wide' declares 0 otherwise branches and must declare exactly one. Without it a value that matches no comparison wedges the run at this router; with two, which one takes an unmatched value is a coin toss written into the document
